query: I just got married and want to add my spouse. Can I switch from Standard to High at the same time, and how long do I have?
answer:
Yes, you can switch from the Standard Option to the High Option due to marriage, as marriage is a Qualifying Life Event (QLE) that allows for an "Increase Enrollment Type" and a "Change from One Plan to Another" [2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-010.md].

**Timeframe:**
The timeframe for requesting a QLE change is from 31 days before to 60 days after the event [2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-011.md].

**Missing Information:**
The provided documents do not specify the exact effective date for your specific change, only that enrollments and changes made based on a QLE are effective on the first day of the pay period following the one in which BENEFEDS receives the enrollment or change [2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-011.md].

The timeframe for requesting a QLE change is from 31 days before to 60 days after the event. There are two exceptions:

-   You cannot request a new enrollment based on a QLE before the QLE occurs, except for enrollment because of a loss of dental or vision insurance. You must make the change no later than 60 days after the event.

Enrollments and enrollment changes made based on a QLE are effective on the first day of the pay period following the one in which BENEFEDS receives the enrollment or change. BENEFEDS will send you confirmation of your new coverage effective date.

Once you enroll in a plan, your 60-day window for that type of plan ends, even if 60 calendar days have not yet elapsed. That means once you have enrolled in either plan, you cannot change or cancel that particular enrollment until the next open season, unless you experience a QLE that allows such a change or cancellation.

## VA Exception for Cancellation

Generally, you may cancel your enrollment only during the annual open season. However, if you are a FEDVIP enrollee paying premiums on a post-tax basis , and you, your family member, or TRICARE-eligible individual (TEI) family member becomes eligible for VA dental or vision benefits, then you may change your enrollment type or cancel your enrollment within 60 days of receiving notification of VA dental or vision eligibility. This 60-day period may fall outside of open season. VA dental or vision eligibility documentation must be submitted to OPM via the BENEFEDS mailbox (benefedsportal@opm.gov) within 60 days of notification to support the FEDVIP enrollment change or cancellation.

Your cancellation is effective at the end of the day before the date OPM sets as the open season effective date. An eligible family member's coverage also ends upon the effective date of the cancellation.

If you are a FEDVIP enrollee paying premiums on a pre-tax basis, and you, your family member, or TEI family member becomes eligible for VA dental or vision benefits, then you may not change or cancel your FEDVIP enrollment until the next open season.

FEDVIP enrollees can verify if they are paying their premiums on a pre- or post-tax basis by contacting BENEFEDS at 1-877-888-3337, TTY: 711, International: 1-571-730-5942.

## Limited Access Area

When you have double coverage, one plan normally pays its benefits in full as the primary payor and the other plan pays a reduced benefit as the secondary payor.  We will consider any benefits payable by your FEHB/PSHB medical plan before we calculate benefits payable by us. In addition to benefits payable by your FEHB/PSHB medical plan, if you or your covered dependents have other dental coverage, you must tell G.E.H.A.  When we are secondary or tertiary (third) payor, our payment will be the lesser of the following:

-  G.E.H.A's benefits; or
-  The remaining balance which when added to the other carrier(s') payment will not exceed the dentist billed amount or lowest negotiated rate.

There is no change in benefit limits or maximums when we are the secondary payor.

Example: Provider is in-network with both FEDVIP plan and other plan. The provider can collect up to the lowest allowable as payment in full.

Patient responsibility: $123.00 - $119.40 = $3.60

A copayment is a fixed amount of money you pay to the provider when you receive services.

A deductible is a fixed amount of expenses you must incur for certain covered services before we will pay for covered services. Covered charges credited to the deductible are also counted towards the Plan maximum and limitations.

There is no calendar year deductible for High Option or Standard in-network. Standard Option out-of-network services under Class A, B and C are subject to a combined $75 deductible per person, per calendar year.

Coinsurance is the percentage of our allowance that you must pay for your care. We will base this percentage on either the billed charge or the plan allowance, whichever is less.

In-Network

- Class D - 50%

Out-of-Network

- Class A - 25%
- Class B - 50%
- Class C - 70%
-  Class D - 50%

Note: If your provider routinely waives (does not require you to pay) your coinsurance, the provider is misstating the fee and may be violating the law. In this case, when we calculate our share, we will reduce the provider's fee by the amount waived. For example, if your dentist ordinarily charges $100 for a service but routinely waives your 50 percent coinsurance, the actual charge is $50. We will pay $25 (50 percent of the actual charge of $50).

Regarding your specific requests:
*   **Switching from Standard to High:** The provided evidence states that a QLE allows you to "change your enrollment" [2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-009.md], but it does not explicitly state whether you can switch plan options (e.g., from Standard to High) at the same time you add a spouse via a QLE.
*   **Timeframe:** The provided evidence defines a QLE as an event that allows enrollment changes outside of open season [2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-009.md], but it does not state the specific number of days you have to complete these changes following the marriage.

Self Only: A Self Only enrollment covers only you as the enrolled employee or annuitant. You may choose a Self Only enrollment even though you have a family, however, your family members will not be covered under FEDVIP.

Self Plus One: A Self Plus One enrollment covers you as the enrolled employee or annuitant plus one eligible family member whom you specify. Self and Family: A Self and Family enrollment covers you as the enrolled employee or annuitant and all of your eligible family members.  You must list all eligible family members when enrolling.

If you or one of your family members is enrolled in or covered by one FEDVIP plan, that person cannot be enrolled in or covered as a family member by another FEDVIP plan offering the same type of coverage; i.e., you (or covered family members) cannot be covered by two FEDVIP dental plans or two FEDVIP vision plans.

## Stop Health Care Fraud!

Fraud increases the cost of health care for everyone and increases your Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program premium.

Protect Yourself From Fraud - Here are some things that you can do to prevent fraud:

- Do not give your plan identification (ID) number over the telephone or to people you do not know, except to your providers, the plan, BENEFEDS, or OPM.
- Let only the appropriate providers review your clinical record or recommend services.
- Avoid using providers who say that an item or service is not usually covered, but they know how to bill us to get it paid.
- Carefully review your explanation of benefits (EOBs) statements.
- Do not ask your provider to make false entries on certificates, bills or records in order to get us to pay for an item or service.
- If you suspect that a provider has charged you for services you did not receive, billed you twice for the same service, or misrepresented any information, do the following:
-  Call the provider and ask for an explanation. There may be an error.
-  If the provider does not resolve the matter, call 800-356-5803, and explain the situation.
- Do not maintain as a family member on your policy:
-  Your former spouse after a divorce decree or annulment is final (even if a court order stipulates otherwise);
-  Your child over age 22 (unless they are disabled and incapable of self- support); or
-  For TRICARE Retiree enrollees: Your child over age 21 or age 23 if a full-time student.

If you have any questions about the eligibility of a dependent, please contact BENEFEDS.

Be sure to review Section 1, Eligibility, of this brochure prior to submitting your enrollment or obtaining benefits.

Fraud or intentional misrepresentation of material fact is prohibited under the Plan. You can be prosecuted for fraud and your agency may take action against you if you falsify a claim to obtain FEDVIP benefits or try to obtain services for someone who is not an eligible family member or who is no longer enrolled in the plan, or enroll in the plan when you are no longer eligible.

## Alternate Benefit

## Dental Review

In some cases, you and your dental practitioner have a choice of treatment options.  In an effort to keep your dental premiums affordable and assure you have coverage for the most common types of dental treatment, the dental plan limits benefits to the maximum allowable charge for the least costly covered service that accomplishes a result that meets accepted standards of professional dental care as determined by us.

If you or your dental practitioner should choose a more costly treatment or service, we will limit benefits payable to the benefit that would have been payable if the least costly covered service had been provided.  This is called the alternate benefit.  Any difference between the alternate benefit and the charge actually incurred is your responsibility, including any applicable coinsurance.  In Section 5, services listed with an asterisk (*) often have the choice of a lower cost treatment.  If you or your dental provider should choose this treatment or service, we will allow the lower cost alternative benefit unless evidence is submitted with the bill to explain why the less expensive treatment could not be done.

We decide the alternative benefit for covered services when we receive the claim.  To avoid incurring expenses we will not cover, we encourage you to request a predetermination of benefits before treatment begins.

Some services require additional information in order to determine if the services are covered or subject to an alternative benefit.  The tooth number is required with claim submission to avoid claim processing delays.  Radiographic images are required for crowns, periodontal procedures, inlays/onlays, anterior and multiple restorations, crown build-ups and implants.  The complete treatment plan is also needed for implants. Charting is required for periodontal procedures.  The date (month and year) of prior placement is required for replacement dentures, partials, crowns and bridges.  The degree and classification of malocclusion is required for orthodontics.

Crown - A pre-operative bitewing and periapical radiographs are required to determine if services meet benefit guidelines for coverage. Date (month and year) of any prior crown is required, if replacement.

Implant - Radiographic images of full arch or panoramic radiographic image are required for implants along with the treatment plan for replacing all missing teeth and teeth that require extraction. Date (month and year) of any prior prosthesis replacing tooth/teeth to be replaced with implant(s).

Orthodontics - The degree and classification of malocclusion is required for orthodontics as follows:

- Classification of malocclusion (this means Class I, II, III), including narrative
-  Degree of overjet, in mm
-  Degree of overbite, in mm
-  Anterior crowding discrepancy in mm
-  Anterior spacing discrepancy in mm
- Description, if any, of cross bite
-  Total number of months required for treatment
-  Treatment objective
-  Cephalometric image or tracing, if available
-  Panoramic radiographic image
-  Diagnostic photos

Periodontal - Full mouth or panoramic radiographs including current bitewing radiographs, periodontal charting, provider narrative and any additional diagnostic information necessary to determine if services meet benefit guidelines for coverage.

By submitting this information with your claim, you may avoid claim processing delays.

## Coordination of Benefits

To obtain a pre-determination, the dentist should submit a completed dental pre-treatment estimate claim form that itemizes the proposed procedure codes, charge for each procedure along with a pre-treatment plan, radiographic image and any other diagnostic materials.

When you visit a provider who participates with both your FEHB/PSHB plan and your FEDVIP plan, the FEHB/PSHB plan will pay benefits first. In these cases, the FEDVIP plan's allowable will be the lesser of: (a) the negotiated allowable charge between the FEDVIP plan and the provider; or (b) the negotiated allowable charge between the FEHB/ PSHB plan and the provider.

You are responsible for the difference between the total FEHB/PSHB and FEDVIP payments and the allowable as defined above.

We are responsible for facilitating the process with the primary FEHB/PSHB first payor.

Self Only: A Self Only enrollment covers only you as the enrolled employee or annuitant. You may choose a Self Only enrollment even though you have a family, however, your family members will not be covered under FEDVIP.

Self Plus One: A Self Plus One enrollment covers you as the enrolled employee or annuitant plus one eligible family member whom you specify. Self and Family: A Self and Family enrollment covers you as the enrolled employee or annuitant and all of your eligible family members.  You must list all eligible family members when enrolling.

If you or one of your family members is enrolled in or covered by one FEDVIP plan, that person cannot be enrolled in or covered as a family member by another FEDVIP plan offering the same type of coverage; i.e., you (or covered family members) cannot be covered by two FEDVIP dental plans or two FEDVIP vision plans.

## Stop Health Care Fraud!

Fraud increases the cost of health care for everyone and increases your Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program premium.

Protect Yourself From Fraud - Here are some things that you can do to prevent fraud:

- Do not give your plan identification (ID) number over the telephone or to people you do not know, except to your providers, the plan, BENEFEDS, or OPM.
- Let only the appropriate providers review your clinical record or recommend services.
- Avoid using providers who say that an item or service is not usually covered, but they know how to bill us to get it paid.
- Carefully review your explanation of benefits (EOBs) statements.
- Do not ask your provider to make false entries on certificates, bills or records in order to get us to pay for an item or service.
- If you suspect that a provider has charged you for services you did not receive, billed you twice for the same service, or misrepresented any information, do the following:
-  Call the provider and ask for an explanation. There may be an error.
-  If the provider does not resolve the matter, call 800-356-5803, and explain the situation.
- Do not maintain as a family member on your policy:
-  Your former spouse after a divorce decree or annulment is final (even if a court order stipulates otherwise);
-  Your child over age 22 (unless they are disabled and incapable of self- support); or
-  For TRICARE Retiree enrollees: Your child over age 21 or age 23 if a full-time student.

If you have any questions about the eligibility of a dependent, please contact BENEFEDS.

Be sure to review Section 1, Eligibility, of this brochure prior to submitting your enrollment or obtaining benefits.

Fraud or intentional misrepresentation of material fact is prohibited under the Plan. You can be prosecuted for fraud and your agency may take action against you if you falsify a claim to obtain FEDVIP benefits or try to obtain services for someone who is not an eligible family member or who is no longer enrolled in the plan, or enroll in the plan when you are no longer eligible.

## Alternate Benefit

## Dental Review

In some cases, you and your dental practitioner have a choice of treatment options.  In an effort to keep your dental premiums affordable and assure you have coverage for the most common types of dental treatment, the dental plan limits benefits to the maximum allowable charge for the least costly covered service that accomplishes a result that meets accepted standards of professional dental care as determined by us.

If you or your dental practitioner should choose a more costly treatment or service, we will limit benefits payable to the benefit that would have been payable if the least costly covered service had been provided.  This is called the alternate benefit.  Any difference between the alternate benefit and the charge actually incurred is your responsibility, including any applicable coinsurance.  In Section 5, services listed with an asterisk (*) often have the choice of a lower cost treatment.  If you or your dental provider should choose this treatment or service, we will allow the lower cost alternative benefit unless evidence is submitted with the bill to explain why the less expensive treatment could not be done.

We decide the alternative benefit for covered services when we receive the claim.  To avoid incurring expenses we will not cover, we encourage you to request a predetermination of benefits before treatment begins.

Some services require additional information in order to determine if the services are covered or subject to an alternative benefit.  The tooth number is required with claim submission to avoid claim processing delays.  Radiographic images are required for crowns, periodontal procedures, inlays/onlays, anterior and multiple restorations, crown build-ups and implants.  The complete treatment plan is also needed for implants. Charting is required for periodontal procedures.  The date (month and year) of prior placement is required for replacement dentures, partials, crowns and bridges.  The degree and classification of malocclusion is required for orthodontics.

Crown - A pre-operative bitewing and periapical radiographs are required to determine if services meet benefit guidelines for coverage. Date (month and year) of any prior crown is required, if replacement.

Implant - Radiographic images of full arch or panoramic radiographic image are required for implants along with the treatment plan for replacing all missing teeth and teeth that require extraction. Date (month and year) of any prior prosthesis replacing tooth/teeth to be replaced with implant(s).

Orthodontics - The degree and classification of malocclusion is required for orthodontics as follows:

- Classification of malocclusion (this means Class I, II, III), including narrative
-  Degree of overjet, in mm
-  Degree of overbite, in mm
-  Anterior crowding discrepancy in mm
-  Anterior spacing discrepancy in mm
- Description, if any, of cross bite
-  Total number of months required for treatment
-  Treatment objective
-  Cephalometric image or tracing, if available
-  Panoramic radiographic image
-  Diagnostic photos

Periodontal - Full mouth or panoramic radiographs including current bitewing radiographs, periodontal charting, provider narrative and any additional diagnostic information necessary to determine if services meet benefit guidelines for coverage.

By submitting this information with your claim, you may avoid claim processing delays.

When you visit a provider who participates with both your FEHB/PSHB plan and your FEDVIP plan, the FEHB/PSHB plan will pay benefits first. To obtain a pre-determination, the dentist should submit a completed dental pre-treatment estimate claim form that itemizes the proposed procedure codes, charge for each procedure along with a pre-treatment plan, radiographic image and any other diagnostic materials.

When you visit a provider who participates with both your FEHB/PSHB plan and your FEDVIP plan, the FEHB/PSHB plan will pay benefits first. In these cases, the FEDVIP plan's allowable will be the lesser of: (a) the negotiated allowable charge between the FEDVIP plan and the provider; or (b) the negotiated allowable charge between the FEHB/ PSHB plan and the provider.

You are responsible for the difference between the total FEHB/PSHB and FEDVIP payments and the allowable as defined above.

We are responsible for facilitating the process with the primary FEHB/PSHB first payor.

## Alternate Benefit

## Dental Review

In some cases, you and your dental practitioner have a choice of treatment options.  In an effort to keep your dental premiums affordable and assure you have coverage for the most common types of dental treatment, the dental plan limits benefits to the maximum allowable charge for the least costly covered service that accomplishes a result that meets accepted standards of professional dental care as determined by us.

If you or your dental practitioner should choose a more costly treatment or service, we will limit benefits payable to the benefit that would have been payable if the least costly covered service had been provided.  This is called the alternate benefit.  Any difference between the alternate benefit and the charge actually incurred is your responsibility, including any applicable coinsurance.  In Section 5, services listed with an asterisk (*) often have the choice of a lower cost treatment.  If you or your dental provider should choose this treatment or service, we will allow the lower cost alternative benefit unless evidence is submitted with the bill to explain why the less expensive treatment could not be done.

We decide the alternative benefit for covered services when we receive the claim.  To avoid incurring expenses we will not cover, we encourage you to request a predetermination of benefits before treatment begins.

Some services require additional information in order to determine if the services are covered or subject to an alternative benefit.  The tooth number is required with claim submission to avoid claim processing delays.  Radiographic images are required for crowns, periodontal procedures, inlays/onlays, anterior and multiple restorations, crown build-ups and implants.  The complete treatment plan is also needed for implants. Charting is required for periodontal procedures.  The date (month and year) of prior placement is required for replacement dentures, partials, crowns and bridges.  The degree and classification of malocclusion is required for orthodontics.

Crown - A pre-operative bitewing and periapical radiographs are required to determine if services meet benefit guidelines for coverage. Date (month and year) of any prior crown is required, if replacement.

Implant - Radiographic images of full arch or panoramic radiographic image are required for implants along with the treatment plan for replacing all missing teeth and teeth that require extraction. Date (month and year) of any prior prosthesis replacing tooth/teeth to be replaced with implant(s).

Orthodontics - The degree and classification of malocclusion is required for orthodontics as follows:

- Classification of malocclusion (this means Class I, II, III), including narrative
-  Degree of overjet, in mm
-  Degree of overbite, in mm
-  Anterior crowding discrepancy in mm
-  Anterior spacing discrepancy in mm
- Description, if any, of cross bite
-  Total number of months required for treatment
-  Treatment objective
-  Cephalometric image or tracing, if available
-  Panoramic radiographic image
-  Diagnostic photos

Periodontal - Full mouth or panoramic radiographs including current bitewing radiographs, periodontal charting, provider narrative and any additional diagnostic information necessary to determine if services meet benefit guidelines for coverage.

By submitting this information with your claim, you may avoid claim processing delays.

query: High says its annual maximum is unlimited. Does that mean implants and braces have no limits?
answer:
No, implants and braces do not have unlimited coverage under the High Option. While the High Option has an unlimited annual benefit maximum for combined Class A, B, and C services [2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-018.md], specific limitations apply to these services:

*   **Implants:** Implant services are limited to an annual maximum of $2,500 per covered person [2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-027.md]. This limit is included in the annual benefit maximum [2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-027.md, 2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-051.md].
*   **Braces (Orthodontics/Class D):** Orthodontic services are subject to a lifetime benefit maximum of $3,500 per person for the High Option [2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-018.md, 2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-036.md].

**Missing Information:** The evidence does not specify if the $2,500 implant limit applies differently to in-network versus out-of-network providers for the High Option, though it notes the limit is "per person per year in-network or out-of-network" [2026-geha-dental-benefits-guide_pages/page-005.md].

answer:

The provided documents do not specify if there are any other specific limitations or exclusions for braces or implants beyond the mentioned annual and lifetime maximums.

*   **Braces (Orthodontics):** Orthodontic services (Class D) are subject to a $3,500 lifetime maximum per person [2026-geha-dental-benefits-guide_pages/page-005.md, 2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-018.md].

## Stop Health Care Fraud!

Fraud increases the cost of health care for everyone and increases your Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program premium.

Protect Yourself From Fraud - Here are some things that you can do to prevent fraud:

- Do not give your plan identification (ID) number over the telephone or to people you do not know, except to your providers, the plan, BENEFEDS, or OPM.
- Let only the appropriate providers review your clinical record or recommend services.
- Avoid using providers who say that an item or service is not usually covered, but they know how to bill us to get it paid.
- Carefully review your explanation of benefits (EOBs) statements.
- Do not ask your provider to make false entries on certificates, bills or records in order to get us to pay for an item or service.
- If you suspect that a provider has charged you for services you did not receive, billed you twice for the same service, or misrepresented any information, do the following:
-  Call the provider and ask for an explanation. There may be an error.
-  If the provider does not resolve the matter, call 800-356-5803, and explain the situation.
- Do not maintain as a family member on your policy:
-  Your former spouse after a divorce decree or annulment is final (even if a court order stipulates otherwise);
-  Your child over age 22 (unless they are disabled and incapable of self- support); or
-  For TRICARE Retiree enrollees: Your child over age 21 or age 23 if a full-time student.

If you have any questions about the eligibility of a dependent, please contact BENEFEDS.

Be sure to review Section 1, Eligibility, of this brochure prior to submitting your enrollment or obtaining benefits.

Fraud or intentional misrepresentation of material fact is prohibited under the Plan. You can be prosecuted for fraud and your agency may take action against you if you falsify a claim to obtain FEDVIP benefits or try to obtain services for someone who is not an eligible family member or who is no longer enrolled in the plan, or enroll in the plan when you are no longer eligible.

## Introduction

On December 23, 2004, President George W. Bush signed the Federal Employee Dental and Vision Benefits Enhancement Act of 2004 (Public Law 108-496). The law directed the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to establish supplemental dental and vision benefit programs to be made available to Federal employees, annuitants and their eligible family members. In response to the legislation, OPM established the Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program (FEDVIP). OPM has contracted with dental and vision insurers to offer an array of choices to Federal employees and annuitants. Section 715 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017 (FY 2017 NDAA), Public Law 114-38, expanded FEDVIP eligibility to certain TRICARE-eligible individuals.

This brochure describes the benefits of G.E.H.A Connection Dental Federal ®  under Government Employees Health Association, Inc.'s contract OPM02-FEDVIP-02AP-08 with OPM, as authorized by the FEDVIP law. The address for our administrative office is:

-  Your child over age 22 (unless they are disabled and incapable of self- support); or
-  For TRICARE Retiree enrollees: Your child over age 21 or age 23 if a full-time student.

If you have any questions about the eligibility of a dependent, please contact BENEFEDS.

Be sure to review Section 1, Eligibility, of this brochure prior to submitting your enrollment or obtaining benefits.

Fraud or intentional misrepresentation of material fact is prohibited under the Plan. You can be prosecuted for fraud and your agency may take action against you if you falsify a claim to obtain FEDVIP benefits or try to obtain services for someone who is not an eligible family member or who is no longer enrolled in the plan, or enroll in the plan when you are no longer eligible.

query: I am becoming eligible for VA dental benefits. Can I cancel GEHA now, or does how I pay my premiums matter?
answer:
Whether you can cancel GEHA depends on how you pay your premiums:

*   **If you pay on a post-tax basis:** You may cancel your enrollment within 60 days of receiving notification of your VA dental eligibility [2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-011.md]. To support this cancellation, VA dental eligibility documentation must be submitted to OPM via the BENEFEDS mailbox (benefedsportal@opm.gov) within 60 days of notification [2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-011.md].
*   **If you pay on a pre-tax basis:** You may **not** change or cancel your FEDVIP enrollment until the next open season [2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-011.md].

You can verify whether you pay your premiums on a pre- or post-tax basis by contacting BENEFEDS at 1-877-888-3337 [2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-011.md].

**Missing Information:**
The provided documents do not state whether your specific current premium payment method is pre-tax or post-tax.

query: Are glasses, hearing aids, and gym memberships covered by dental insurance, or are they discounts?
answer:
Glasses, hearing aids, and gym memberships are provided as discounts/value-added benefits rather than covered insurance benefits.

*   **Glasses (Vision):** Connection Vision provides "low copays for eye exams and discounts on lenses, frames and contact lenses" [2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-049.md]. Specifically, members can get "30%-60% off TruHearing ® hearing aids" [2026-geha-dental-benefits-guide_pages/page-009.md].

These benefits are "neither offered nor guaranteed under contract with the FEDVIP Program" but are made available to G.E.H.A. members and their eligible family members [2026-geha-dental-plan-brochure_pages/page-049.md], [2026-geha-dental-benefits-guide_pages/page-009.md].

## Section 4 Your Cost For Covered Services

This is what you will pay out-of-pocket for covered care:

## Copayment

Deductible

## Coinsurance

A copayment is a fixed amount of money you pay to the provider when you receive services.

- G.E.H.A Connection Dental Federal ® High Option - no copay.

G.E.H.A Connection Dental Federal ® Standard Option - no copay.

A deductible is a fixed amount of expenses you must incur for certain covered services before we will pay for covered services. Covered charges credited to the deductible are also counted towards the Plan maximum and limitations.

There is no calendar year deductible for High Option or Standard in-network. Standard Option out-of-network services under Class A, B and C are subject to a combined $75 deductible per person, per calendar year.

Coinsurance is the percentage of our allowance that you must pay for your care. We will base this percentage on either the billed charge or the plan allowance, whichever is less.

For High Option your coinsurance is as follows:

-  Class A - nothing
-  Class B - 20%
-  Class C - 50%
-  Class D - 30%

For Standard Option your coinsurance is as follows:

In-Network

- Class A - nothing
- Class B - 45%
- Class C - 65%
- Class D - 50%

Out-of-Network

- Class A - 25%
- Class B - 50%
- Class C - 70%
-  Class D - 50%

Note: If your provider routinely waives (does not require you to pay) your coinsurance, the provider is misstating the fee and may be violating the law. In this case, when we calculate our share, we will reduce the provider's fee by the amount waived. For example, if your dentist ordinarily charges $100 for a service but routinely waives your 50 percent coinsurance, the actual charge is $50. We will pay $25 (50 percent of the actual charge of $50).
